Front: One minute of tape, two scores — name the axes and what each counts.
Back: Effort = contracts changing hands (unsigned participation). Effect = price movement produced. Cross them day-relative and the minute lands in one of four cells: F1 conviction / F2 absorption / F3 hollow / F4 dead.

Front: A minute travels 5 points but closes where it opened. Which number catches this, and what does it mean?
Back: Travel-ratio (displacement ÷ travel) near 0 — a round trip: a fight that ended where it started, not stillness. Displacement alone would score it "no effect."

Front: Where does the 1-minute lens hide half the day's violence?
Back: Inside F2 absorption cells: 50.6% of range-travel is invisible to displacement, and 82.5% of that hides in F2 minutes. Absorption minutes are internally violent wars, not quiet ones.

Front: Why is force (signed delta) recorded on every atom but NOT a matrix axis?
Back: Effort answers "how much business," force answers "which side pressed" — different quantities. Keeping them separate is what lets the counterforce-leg exist: price moving THROUGH opposing force.

Front: Graded F1 at 0.62 versus "is F1" — why does the wording matter?
Back: The 2×2 grid is imposed on a smooth surface (no natural clusters). Cell membership is a coordinate, not an identity; the grade says how far from the boundary the label sits.

Front: What must you say when a label falls in the coin-flip grade-band?
Back: The straddled pair, never the bare cell — "F3/F4 coin-flip." One classification in five sits there (20.4% of atoms); reporting the pair is the vocabulary being honest, not failing.

Front: Cutpoint versus threshold.
Back: Cutpoints SORT (pace 0.75 divides flush-leg from steady-leg; the grade measures distance from it). Thresholds ACT (the reversal threshold ends a leg; 150 contracts of delta fires the flip-stage). Bare "cut" stays reserved for cutting a position.

Front: Describe the zigzag decomposition in one breath.
Back: Redraw the day with the fewest alternating pen strokes that capture every swing bigger than the reversal threshold (20% of the day's final range). Each stroke is a leg; sub-threshold wiggle is absorbed into the leg as texture.

Front: Why is 7/22's 4-point opening trap at 7533 not its own leg?
Back: The day's reversal threshold was 7.65 pts; a 4-pt excursion is under threshold, so it lives INSIDE leg 1 as atom-scale texture. Structure below the threshold is the atoms' job, not the zigzag's.

Front: Name the two big-leg facts that matter for fly entries.
Back: Big legs keep what they take (flush-leg median giveback 5% — the extreme tends to hold), and legs die hot (pivot-atoms grade F1 conviction 63% — turns are killed by opposition, not faded). Honest exception: 37% of pivots are quiet.

Front: Falling price, blue (buy-dominant) footers. Which archetype, and which standing watch applies?
Back: Counterforce-leg — price falling through net buying, trapped buyers all the way down (specimen: 2026-07-27 open, −81.75 pts on +3,033 delta). Direction Inversion Watch territory by construction: name the direction anchor out loud.

Front: What is dead-drift, and why does the taxonomy keep such a boring name?
Back: The residual majority: 32.4% of legs are nothing happening. Naming the nothing honestly is what makes the other seven names mean something.

Front: Thrust, parry — then what? Name the two stories and the discipline.
Back: Parry FAILS → micro-stall (pause inside a living leg, conviction resumes). Parry HOLDS and force turns → stall-stage (the leg dying into a possible trap). Indistinguishable in the moment; the next atoms decide. The discipline is sitting with the ambiguity instead of resolving it early.

Front: 7/22 afternoon: atoms nearly all F4-dead, the leg grades F1. Contradiction?
Back: No — tiers measure different things. 221 minutes of small efforts SUM to corpus-scale mass; atom grades are day-relative texture, leg grades are corpus-wide. Speaking rule: say which tier you mean.

Front: Your old words — sweep, absorption, divergence. Replaced?
Back: Kept, addressed: they are episode-tier primitives (sweep-print, absorption-read, delta-divergence) — the LIVE tier, machine-emitted, exactly where they always were. The taxonomy gave every word an address; it took none away.

Front: Which tier do your yea/nay decisions ride on, and why?
Back: The LIVE tier only — stages, primitives, confirmation-events, raw atom fields. Every percentile, cell, archetype, and leg boundary is HINDSIGHT (needs the completed day); hindsight grades the tape, it never asks you for a decision.

Front: The V-signature wins 77.5% vs 46.9% base. Why is it not a live entry rule?
Back: Both inputs are hindsight: percentiles rank against the COMPLETED day, and a leg pivot exists only after the retracement proves it. Turning it live needs developing-day percentiles and provisional pivots — open engineering. Until then it grades trades; it doesn't take them.

Front: Host-leg direction splits confirmation win rates how — and what may you do with that today?
Back: 66% with the host leg vs 19% against it — the strongest single separator found. It is a HINDSIGHT diagnostic: use it to grade and study, not to enter. "Don't fade the leg" becomes measurable, not yet tradeable.

Front: Why did "band" need a partner word?
Back: It crosses domains: VWAP-bands are price envelopes on the chart; grade-bands are certainty stripes on a label. Same word, two referents on the same desk — so bare "band" is banned and the compound carries the sense. (Steve's catch.)

Front: The narrative said archetypes "sat this day out" yet gave sightings. What was wrong, and what is the rule?
Back: The sightings were from OTHER corpus days and the prose didn't say so — a provenance ambiguity. Rule: every claim wears its origin; a sentence that knows where its evidence came from must say it.

Front: Silhouette — is it vocabulary?
Back: No. It was coach improvisation, never defined in any surface — the exact failure the lexicon exists to prevent. If a word is worth using, it enters lexicon.yaml first; the linter enforces the rest.

Front: An agent said your fly "expired worthless" twelve minutes before the close. What rule was broken and what is the fix?
Back: Liveness at statement time: market outcomes before the bell are forecasts, not facts — no settlement claims pre-close; phrase as probability with "as of <time>". (An index quoting no bid/ask proves nothing about the clock — indexes never quote one.)

Front: An accuracy briefing says "423 signals across 182 days." You only studied 7/24. What are the 182 days?
Back: The backtest: the software replayed over all stored history (182 scorable days), graded as if watching live. Accuracy numbers always come from the whole corpus — one day's handful of signals proves nothing.

Front: What is an anchor, in one sentence?
Back: A price level the software is told to watch — almost always a level from the letter. The recognizer sees nothing but the tape and its anchors.

Front: Fire #4 at the same level: buy signals win 31%. Steve's instinct: "flip it." Why is that instinct legitimate here?
Back: The scoring race is symmetric (±5 first-touch), so a 31% long literally is a 69% short by the same rule. The fade held in both time halves and strengthens with depth (75% by fire #6). Caveats: really ~17 clustered days, not in the first hour, and a 5-point race is not a trade plan. (Bead: Fade The Fourth Fire.)

Front: Where does the signal edge concentrate in the day, and where does it die?
Back: Concentrates: first hour (54% wins, typical winner ~13 pts — the day's best slice). Dies: midday — the noon hour wins 18%, hour 10 wins 27%. Lunch chop kills the pattern.

Front: A level fires its first signal of the day. How much should you trust it, and what changed in 2026?
Back: Less than you'd think: fire #1 won 59% in older data but only 37% since June — the largest unexplained drift in the system. Treat "first touch is the clean one" as an open question, not a rule.

Front: Does the recognition engine see market internals (TICK, breadth)?
Back: No — it reads only the ES tape and its anchor levels. Internals live in a separate instrument (the MI gauge, −100..+100 with a named driver) built for the trader's eyes; joining the two streams is an open measured question.

Front: The scoring rule grades a signal "loss" even though price later rallied 15 points. Why keep such a harsh rule?
Back: First-touch ±5 measures call quality with zero judgment calls: did the trade work before it hurt? Softening the rule would smuggle trade management into a measurement of the machine. P&L is a separate question that belongs to sizing — the trader's seat.

Front: What does "held out-of-sample" actually claim about a pattern? (hunt-pile / drawer-pile)
Back: Patterns are hunted only in the OLDER half of the stored days; the recent half stays locked in a drawer. A finished rule must then work on the drawer days it never saw. Works there = likely real market behavior; only worked where we hunted = memorized coincidence, thrown out however good it looked. Snag card 07-31: term first landed as jargon.

Front: In "graded F2" — what does the F stand for, and where did the codes come from?
Back: F is for FRAME: the drill catalog's Part II frame scenarios — one paused bar, "what is happening in this cell?" Siblings: S1-S6 (level-engagement Scenarios), T1-T3 (Tempo). The 07-28 taxonomy inherited the already-ratified drill names instead of minting new ones, so "graded F2" = this bar read through drill frame #2, absorption. Snag card 07-31: origin was stated nowhere.

Front: A 4-point counter-move hits mid-leg (like the 7533 opening trap on 7/22). When does a backtrack become its own leg — and where does it go when it doesn't?
Back: The pen turns only for a backtrack bigger than ~20% of the day's FINAL range (~8 pts on 7/22). Smaller: the pen keeps going — the wiggle's minutes stay on the tape, fully graded, inside the leg as texture (why travel > displacement, why giveback exists). 4 < 8, so the trap lives inside the opening leg. Sting: final-range threshold = the map is drawn only in hindsight. Snag card 07-31.

Front: Name the three nested tiers, the tier that stands BESIDE them, and why it stands beside.
Back: Nested by TIME: atoms (minutes) inside legs (zigzag strokes) inside the day (its legs in order = the day-sequence). The axes (effort/effect/force) are rulers, not a tier — they measure atoms and legs alike. BESIDE the stack: the episode — one whole fight at one price LEVEL, first contact to resolution — because it slices by place, not time; one level's fight can span pieces of several legs. It is the recognizer's LIVE tier (stages, primitives, 2,000-CONTRACT bars); legs/day-sequence are hindsight maps. Snag card 07-31.

Front: A buy confirmation fires. What is its host-leg, what changes when the call is WITH vs AGAINST it — and why can't you trade this split live?
Back: Host-leg = the zigzag stroke the signal's minute lands inside. Buy call inside a rising stroke: 66% win (±5 first-touch, 30 min; typical 10.9 for / 5.0 against). Inside a falling stroke — a bottom-call mid-drop: 19% (3.4 for / 11.2 against). Not tradeable live because legs are drawn AFTER the close (final-range threshold, pivots confirmed by retracement) — 66/19 is autopsy, the live provisional-pivot version is unshipped engineering. Snag card 07-31.
